pitch_detail.notes: Mix of scrambling, tree navigation, and variable rock quality leading toward the ridge crest; can be linked.
Splitter hand crack, widely noted as excellent climbing.
Double/twin cracks — the technical crux of the route.
Layback and wide corner, with multiple line options.
Long pitch on a splitter along the crest; prone to rope drag if not managed.
Twin cracks leading toward the final pitch.
A widening crack, then exposed face climbing up and left — the route's "mental crux" — runout with marginal protection.
40m warm-up pitch, left-facing corner to a stance below left-slanting twin cracks
50m diagonal twin cracks with an inset dihedral crux; squeaky-clean rock
50m, layback-undercling-stem up a leaning corner crack past yellow flakes to a burly exit
20m, crux — short arch, well-bolted pocket climbing, exit move onto the Supercave
30m, steep exit from the left side of the cave via an overhanging wall; often called the hardest pitch
56m, steep face of flakes, corners and ramps to the wall top
optional 15m finish to a tree
Long and a little runout overall, though the hardest 5.8 sections have better protection.
Chimney climbing with runout sections on sub-par, grainy rock.
Continues the chimney system on grainy rock with runout moves.
One of the better pitches on the route, ending on a large ledge.
Crux pitch with limited, funky protection; some sections cannot be pulled through on gear alone.
Second crux pitch, similarly sparse/funky protection; dangerous rope drag noted.
V-slot that mellows out dramatically toward the summit.
210', left-facing corner from the Tiger's start, ending below a roof at a pin/gear anchor
40', first crux — stem moves and a dyno to a huge bucket, then dirty 5.10 above
190', traverse left to a crack system leading to a large treed ledge
100', standout pitch — elegant flake climbing and powerful moves on clean edges
150', face climbing with a lieback corner, traverses into the cave system
105', wandering pitch, unprotected/run-out terrain below a roof
130', memorable hand-traverse pitch connecting to the Ellen Pea route
180', finish via hollow, grainy flakes; rappel or scramble off
Slab rambling in a corner over a few roofs to a 2-bolt belay.
Overlapping flakes/roofs, underclinging to a stem-box belay at two offset bolts.
'The Numbah 9 pitch' — corner to a cruxy flare section, 2-bolt belay.
Hand crack to a bolt, past suspect rock through two bolts, 2-bolt anchor.
Left-leaning seams on subpar rock quality.
Signature splitter headwall — lieback to bolt, then 15-20 hard sustained finger-locking moves; single-bolt belay backed by cam.
Shares start with Peanuts to Serve You - climb that route for pitch 1.
Continue up corner, finger-to-hand crack up and left; short but pumpy.
Route crux; crack starts wide, narrows to finger pockets; easier 5.9-5.10c variations exist.
Short chimney on left through forest to belay below large corner.
Long and sustained; ramps and corners, finishes with a one-move dyno for the top.
Handcrack (sometimes wet), traverse to bolted belay in a right-facing corner.
Jam/lieback the corner crack to another bolted belay.
Crux; up and right around a roof, back left into a corner, delicate footwork to a bolted belay ledge.
55m. Open book with a rightward slab traverse into a dual-cracked corner.
25m. Treed-ledge approach, then a left-slanting crack into a corner; a variation exists around 5.10. Watch for loose rock, including stacked blocks near the top.
40m. Hand crack leading to face climbing and a left-facing dihedral.
25m. The 'money pitch' - a tips corner with laybacking.
45m. Traverse into a steep right-facing hand crack/layback corner.
Easy, wandering terrain to the summit.
